notes:
Pilot: started from lawyer.json ("from": "lawyer"). Why: a notary's work runs like the lawyer's signings, not a lockout or a repair: papers signed at home, a hospital or a care home, every signer's photo ID checked and the signer met directly, witnesses, video sessions in flow A, private papers kept off texts, no legal advice. The lawyer's own parts were taken out: the conflict check (A4-43/B4-38 form, A6-16/B6-15 expert), the no-$2 rule, the trust-money offs, the confidentiality agreement and named-only (notary work pays the $2 and is rated). Its rename list was rebuilt from the master, with the lawyer's as a checklist.
Usual side: flow B, a mobile signing (the old flowchart's whole story: a notary sent to a care home). Flow A: Sam's second company, Main Street Notary, an office with walk-ins and video signings. Video signings count as flow A (TWO-FLOWS.md), only where the state's form allows them and the notary holds the online authorization.
Money paths, from the old flowchart and the plug-in: B list|card|card (a card saved on the secure page, charged at DONE for the signatures and the travel fee; cash recorded with 'paid cash'). A list|none|counter (office: nothing taken, paid at the front desk) and list|none|bill (video: no front desk, so Rosie texts the bill). Not listed: holds, deposits and full prices (a notary takes nothing before), photos and quotes at the visit (every price is the list: per signature and the travel fee), the business's own way (loan signings are paid by title companies, outside Rosie). The old flowchart saved a card for video sessions too; with no fee ever charged for a missed video signing, the bill does the same with nothing saved.
Prices are the example businesses' own, never a state's: $15 a notarized signature (always under the state's cap, a switch), Lee Mobile Notary's $89 travel fee, a $25 witness, Main Street Notary's $45 travel fee. Alex's home signing: 6 signatures + travel = $179 (the master's number). Office: 2 signatures = $30 (the master's $35 renamed in flow A).
Fees: only the travel fee, at the customer's place, for a cancel after 7am that day, nobody there, or a signer who can't sign (no valid ID); Sam confirms each; only where the state's form allows a travel fee then (a switch: S1-14, S1-21, B5-05, B7-10, pf.money, pf.rules), and where it allows only the miles driven, that's the limit. No cancel or no-show fee at the office or by video. No tips (a notary may charge only what the state's form allows). The sign-up words (S1-12 to S1-21, S1-41 to S1-49) set every service this way, so no sign-up example sets a hold, deposit or full price.
Times: a signing starts at a set time (B4-83 keeps '2 A set start time'; arrival windows off). The master's windows are renamed to starts ('arriving 8–10am' to 'starts at 8:30am' and the like). Clock on B: booked Mon 6:48pm, reminder Wed 10am, OMW Thu 8:10am, check-in and ID check 8:30am, DONE 9:15am (about 45 minutes for 6 signatures), receipt 9:20am, rating 11am. A: office at Sat 11:00am; the video bill at 11:20am.
The ID check is the master's 'what Alex was asked to have ready' (B8-45, A8-02): each signer's current photo ID, never photographed; no valid ID goes as 'Can't go ahead' on the customer's side (B8-60: the travel fee only if Sam confirms). B8-18/A8-23 carry the talk with the signer, the complete papers and the signer-picks-the-wording rule; B8-39/A8-43 carry the signing, the certificates and the journal; B8-55/A8-52 say the journal is the notary's own book, never Rosie's.
Not notary work is screened with the master's own steps: a home loan closing (B4-03: ask the title or escrow company), legal questions and help with papers (B3-21, A4-38, B7-16, A7-12: a notary can't give legal advice).
Own steps (flow B, both from the old flowchart): the team's witness can't come (B7-x01 to B7-x04: the customer brings an adult witness the papers allow and the fee is dropped, or moves the time); the care home closes to visitors (B7-x05 to B7-x08: a new day, a video signing booked in flow A, or a free cancel).
Turned off: plans, insurance, packages, gift cards, deposits' rest, damage holds, crews short a person, classes, tables, drop-offs, sent now, nobody home, deliveries, outside checks, permits, items to the shop, right to cancel (a paper notarized on the spot), tips, and the after-visit branches a signing never has (proposals, reports, items left, rentals, aftercare). Kept: walk-ins at the office (a line for the next free notary).
splitsKept A: A7-61 (another commissioned notary stands in; a signing in Spanish has nobody else) and A8-02 (every signer's ID is required, and its absence stops the signing).
Cast: Lee Mobile Notary (500 Lake Ave; notaries Luis, who speaks Spanish and fingerprints, and Kevin, also the witness) and Main Street Notary (310 Main St; Nadia, who speaks Spanish, and Elena; both hold the online authorization). Second kind of work: fingerprinting (a technician's certificate only where the state's form requires one). NEW examples: a document courier (B), passport photos (A). Commission numbers carry this work's own letters (NP, FP).
keep: 'notary', 'notary work', 'travel fee' and 'lawyer' are the lawyer pilot's words but are this work's own (a notary points every legal question to a lawyer).
Every state rule is a switch from the state's form: the fee cap per act and for video acts, the travel-fee limit, the journal and thumbprint, video signings and their platform and witnesses, the 'not an attorney' notice, the banned word 'notario'. The old flowchart's one-state facts (one state's $10 cap, another's miles-only rule, another's notario ban, cited codes) are switches now. Its Calendly, Proof and Snapdocs parts are outdated: Rosie is the software.
Not sure: whether every state lets a mobile notary charge a travel fee for a late cancel (kept as a switch, Sam confirming); whether a paper's own witness may join a video signing (kept as a switch: only where the form allows it); the $15 example is under many states' caps but not all, so the cap check (a gap) matters.
Review Oct 23: a late-cancel travel fee and a witness by video are switches from the state's form in the plug-in and the flows. Same-day signings ask Sam first (S1-21), so S11-01/S11-03 wait for that reason, not for a new customer. Video bills have no office-phone or cash branch (A9-05). Not added: a card saved for video signings (the old flowchart charged the card already saved for the home visit; here a move to video is a new booking billed after, B7-x07).
